card: G3-10k - where a JC3 vehicle body's inertia tensor lives

payload_layouts.name: after_mass_scalar
payload_layouts.where: +0x2c f32 (4 bytes - too small for a tensor)

unknowns: the absolute semantics/units of the decoded diagonal: the box oracle rejects the collision-hull reading on every box body (0/107 at 1%), and the residual is a *uniform* 1.2767 factor, not scatter - so the tensor was authored from geometry the collision hull does not contain. What would settle it: the render mesh of the same part (its convex hull / tetrahedral tensor) compared under the same decode.

the third group (+0x20..+0x27): three lanes whose magnitudes are the largest in the block (all near +-32768) and whose own exponent lane decodes them to ~1e-36, i.e. 'no products'. Whether those lanes are products, a principal axis or a mirror tag is not decoded; the mirror test (pass 1) shows two of them flip sign between left/right parts, which both readings allow.

the bias 111 is a format constant measured to better than one octave (110 and 112 are 2x off); no file in this tree documents the packing, so the exact fixed-point layout of the w lane (floor(w/128) with w = exponent << 7) is derived, not documented. A Havok 2014 header for hkCompressedMassProperties would confirm it.

how the mass at +0x28 relates to the tensor: the box bodies show a uniform 1.275x excess, which is exactly what a 1.275x larger authoring mass *or* 1.13x larger authoring extents would produce; the two cannot be separated without the authoring mesh.

verdict.statement: the payload's second group is the inertia diagonal in the shape frame (value = mantissa * 2**(floor(w/128) - 111), bias pinned by the centre-of-mass group against the hull centroid, median error 0.0156); the brief's box oracle is not met - 0 of 107 single-box fleet bodies match m/12*(b^2+c^2) within 1%, with a uniform 1.2767 excess on all three moments, so the stored tensor belongs to the authoring geometry, not to the collision hull
